title: SLO Symphony: orchestrated preemption for continuous batching with KV cache custodianship
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: As continuous batching grows tenant multiplexing, simple preempt/evict heuristics either breach tail latency SLOs or thrash the KV cache and GPU memory, increasing per-token cost. We need a unified preemption policy that treats preemption as an orchestrated operation — balancing SLO protection, KV residency, and GPU memory fragmentation — rather than binary killing of slices.

Goal: Deliver an SLO-aware preemption controller (the 'SLO Symphony') that: (1) minimizes SLO violations under high contention, (2) preserves high-value KV entries for workloads sensitive to cold-KV penalties, (3) avoids memory fragmentation by coordinating compaction windows, and (4) provides stable, explainable fairness across tenants.

Non-goals: This ticket does not onboard new model architectures or change kernel selection heuristics. It focuses on scheduling and cache/ memory coordination only.
acceptance_criteria: Under synthetic mixed-tenancy workload (80/20 short/long), p95 latency <= configured SLO for P1 tenants and p99 <= SLO + 15ms for best-effort tenants during 95% of intervals over a 1h soak
KV cold-miss amplification reduced by >= 25% compared to current preemptive-kill baseline for long-context customers
GPU memory fragmentation score (as measured by compaction-trigger-rate) reduced by >= 30% during sustained high churn runs
Feature gated behind runtime flag with metrics exposed in Console (preemption_decisions, kv_evicted_keys, compaction_windows), and e2e canary rollout plan defined
Design doc reviewed and approved by Runtime/Platform and ProdOps; at least two integration tests exercising graceful preempt/resume paths
No regression in throughput for throughput-sensitive benchmarks (+/-5% compared to baseline)
Telemetry added: reason-coded preempt events, tenant-score breakdown, time-to-resume, and KV hit-rate differential per tenant
design_notes: Core idea: convert preemption into a choreography — a Preemption Conductor computes a tenant 'urgency' score combining SLO slack, request deadline, KV heatmap, and GPU fragmentation signal. Instead of immediate kill, conductor issues phased actions: (1) soft-throttle, (2) KV holdback or pin hints, (3) compaction-friendly pause, (4) full preempt as last resort.

Urgency scoring: linear combination with tunable weights + entropy penalty to avoid oscillation. We will add an adaptive learnable multiplier that increases weight on KV-heat when empirical cold-KV penalty is high for a tenant.

KV custody: introduce 'custodian hints' on KV entries for tenants about eviction priority. Custodianship lowers eviction probability for entries touched within the tenant's recent critical windows. Hints are advisory and scoped per-GPU to keep metadata small.

Compaction windows: when fragmentation exceeds threshold, conductor schedules short compaction-friendly pauses (20-100ms) aligned to low-urgency tenants. These windows are cooperative and advertised via in-band control messages; runtime coordinates with allocator to minimize fragmentation.

Fairness model: proportional fairness by tenant weight (derived from plan + recent errors) with decay for repeated heavy evictions to prevent starvation. Policy parameters exposed as feature flags for experiments.
Fallback: on severe overload the system may fallback to current emergency preempt path; we will measure how often fallback happens and tune parameters to reduce it.
Observability: add decision traces for each preemption event (score components, KV delta estimate, chosen action, estimated resume time) and sample stack traces for debugging.
Security: no new sensitive data persisted; KV hints are tenant-scoped and ephemeral. Feature gate will be off by default for Private deployments until security review completes.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - Prototype (2 wks): implement simplified conductor in the runtime that computes urgency score and issues soft-throttle + decision trace metric. Unit tests for score math and mock scheduler.
Phase 2 - KV Custodianship (2 wks): add small per-GPU hint table and eviction heuristic that consults hints during GC. Expose kv_evicted_keys and kv_pinned_count telemetry.
Phase 3 - Compaction Coordination (2 wks): allocator hook for compaction windows and in-band pause signaling. Add compaction_window_count metric and fragmentation_score.
Phase 4 - E2E Integration & Load Testing (2 wks): run mixed-tenancy resiliency tests on staging cluster, iterate on weights, and add integration tests for graceful resume and resume after compaction.
Phase 5 - Canary Rollout (2 wks): enable feature-flag by tenant group, observe Console metrics and adjust. Prepare rollback plan and alerting thresholds.
PRs: runtime: github.com/redwood/realtime/pull/6137 (conductor prototype), allocator: github.com/redwood/gpu-alloc/pull/219 (compaction-hooks), kv: github.com/redwood/kv/pull/1123 (custodian-hints)
Docs: update Console docs and ops runbook with decision trace interpretation and rollback steps
notes: This approach is intentionally conservative: phased actions prefer latency preservation over throughput. We expect initial parameter tuning to be the most time-consuming part. Keep default weights tuned for enterprise-tenants initially.
rollout_plan: Canary group: 5% of traffic from non-critical tenants for 48h
Stage 2: 20% including a mix of long-context customers for 72h
Full rollout: enable for all hosted customers with monitoring for 7 days, Private deployments opt-in only after security review
tests: unit: urgency score math, hint table concurrency
integration: staged preempt sequences (soft-throttle -> compaction window -> resume)
load: mixed-tenancy 1000qps soak with tenant weight variation
chaos: random allocation failures to ensure fallback works
